summary: Asana allows developers to register private apps via the developer console. To share apps publicly or with other workspaces, developers must complete a pre-flight checklist, provide test credentials, and submit the app for a review process that typically takes one week.

claim.text: The initial response time for app submissions is aimed to be within one week.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: We aim to provide an initial response on app submissions within one week. However, the review timeline may vary depending on the complexity of the app.

access_ladder.name: Private Development
access_ladder.allows: The app is accessible only to the developer's own workspace.

claims.text: All apps start as private to the developer by default.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: By default, all apps start out private to the developer.

access_ladder.name: Internal Workspace Sharing
access_ladder.allows: The app can be shared with specific workspaces that the developer belongs to.

claims.text: Apps can be shared with specific workspaces that the developer belongs to.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: Sharing your app with specific workspaces allows you to share the app with any workspace(s) that you are a member of.

access_ladder.name: Public Authorization
access_ladder.allows: Users from any Asana workspace can authorize and use the app.

claims.text: Apps can be shared with any workspace, allowing users from any Asana workspace to authorize the app.
claims.label: official_docs
claims.evidence_quote: If your app is intended to be shared with many users, select Any workspace. This will allow users from any Asana workspace to authorize the app if they are given the authorization URL.

claim.text: You must register your application with Asana to receive a client ID and client secret.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: You must first register your application with Asana to receive a client ID and client secret. To do so, first visit the developer console and select Create new app, as shown below:

claim.text: All OAuth apps are created privately by default.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: All OAuth apps are created privately by default.

go_public.item: You must submit your app for review if you want to make it available to users in any…

claim.text: You must submit your app for review if you want to make it available to users in any Asana workspace beyond your own or list it publicly.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Submitting your app for review is not required to obtain a token. You only need to submit your app if you intend to: Make your app available to users in any Asana workspace, beyond your own organization or development environment List your app publicly on the Asana app directory

go_public.item: App names must not include the word Asana to avoid confusion.

claim.text: App names must not include the word Asana to avoid confusion.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: To help users clearly distinguish third-party apps from those built by Asana, app names should not include the word “Asana.” This helps avoid confusion and ensures consistency across our ecosystem.

go_public.item: Developers must provide test account credentials for the review process.

claim.text: Developers must provide test account credentials for the review process.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Provide any test account credentials necessary for your app (this is only used for the review process and will not be published publicly)

go_public.item: A privacy policy URL is required for the app listing.

claim.text: A privacy policy URL is required for the app listing.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Include a privacy policy URL to ensure transparency about how you handle user data and comply with legal requirements.

claim.text: Apps submitted for publication to the app directory must be shared to Any workspace.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: All apps submitted for publication to the app directory must be shared to Any workspace.

claim.text: Calls to the search API are limited to 60 requests per minute.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Calls to the search API are limited to 60 requests per minute.

blockers.issue: Apps cannot be edited once they have been submitted for review.

claim.text: Apps cannot be edited once they have been submitted for review.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Once your app has been submitted on the Submit for review page, the review process will begin. At this point, the app will no longer be open for further edits.

claim.text: Do not share your client secret or include it in source code.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Your client secret is a secret, and it should never be shared with anyone or added into source code that others could gain access to.

claim.text: Requests without PKCE parameters will be rejected for localhost, 127.0.0.1, or native URN redirect URIs.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: OAuth flows that use a localhost, 127.0.0.1, or native URN redirect URI must use PKCE (S256). Include a code_challenge in the authorization request and the matching code_verifier in the token exchange. Requests without these parameters will be rejected.

blockers.issue: Incomplete or substandard listings may result in additional review cycles and delayed…
blockers.fix: Carefully follow all instructions and provide all required information.

claim.text: Incomplete or substandard listings may result in additional review cycles and delayed publication.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Incomplete or substandard listings may result in additional review cycles, slowing down the approval process and limiting your app’s visibility to potential users.

blockers.issue: If the state parameter does not match, your app should return a 422 error.
blockers.fix: Verify that the state that the request is coming from matches the state that you sent earlier.

claim.text: If the state parameter does not match, your app should return a 422 error.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If the state does not match, your app should return a 422 error.

blockers.issue: If the computed signature and x-asana-request-signature do not match, your app server…
blockers.fix: Generate a computed signature based on the request and compare it to the x-asana-request-signature from the request header.

claim.text: If the computed signature and x-asana-request-signature do not match, your app server should return a 400 error.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If the computed signature and x-asana-request-signature do not match, your app server should return a 400 error.

blockers.issue: Your app server should only return a 200 response if the current date and time is before…
blockers.fix: Check the expires_at query parameter value against the current date and time.

claim.text: Your app server should only return a 200 response if the current date and time is before the expires_at time.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Your app server should check this value and only return a 200 response if the current date and time is before the expires_at time.

blockers.issue: Asana OAuth does not support making token requests from a browser for security reasons.
blockers.fix: Use a server-side implementation to manage the OAuth grant flow.

claim.text: Asana OAuth does not support making token requests from a browser for security reasons.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Note: Asana OAuth currently does not support making token requests from a browser for security reasons.
